description: Coordinator hooks — session guardrails and cost optimization. REGISTRATIONS IN THIS FILE ARE READ AT SESSION START AND CACHED: adding or removing an entry here reaches NO already-running session until it runs /reload-plugins or restarts, and a deleted entry keeps firing until then. Run /reload-plugins in this session before testing your change, and expect peer sessions on this machine to keep their booted roster regardless. Hook SCRIPT bodies are unaffected — those resolve live per tool call. Measurement: docs/wiki/external-plugin-live-resolution.md § Hook REGISTRATION staleness; tripwire HOOKS-JSON-REGISTRATION-STALENESS.

SessionStart._comment: SESSIONSTART-DISPATCH FAN-IN (state/audits/2026-08-16-doe-spawn-totality-kill-list.md; state/handoffs/2026-08-16-untitled-6c1eb4ae.md § Next Steps 1) -- the single SYNC SessionStart entrypoint, replacing six of the nine standalone registrations that used to live in this array: the orientation RAM-cache injector (project-orientation.py, PM directive 2026-07-15), the settings.json integrity guard (guard-settings-integrity.py), the foreign-platform-path guard (guard-foreign-platform-paths.py), the C8 write-confinement anchor (session-start-write-bump-anchor.py), and the hook-generation self-probe (guard-hook-generation-self-probe.py). AMENDED 2026-08-29 (chunk C1, docs/plans/2026-08-29-restore-em-boot-payload-delivery.md): C1b EM-role assertion (assert-em-role.py) is NO LONGER among the folded six -- it was unfolded back into its own top-level registration below because riding this fan-in's single shared stdout stream meant its payload was captured but truncated away before reaching a session's actual context in 275 of 279 measured archived sessions. It keeps its original `startup|resume|clear|compact|fork` matcher unchanged. Hosting change only, never a policy change: sessionstart-dispatch.py runs the remaining five in one interpreter, registered on the UNION of their two prior matchers (startup|clear|compact for four of them; startup|resume|clear|compact|fork for the other two -- the other two of the nine prior registrations' four distinct matcher sets, startup|compact for sweep-boot and startup alone for the commit-msg-repair hook, are not folded into this dispatcher; see below), each guard internally gated to its OWN original source set via the SessionStart payload's own `source` field (confirmed present, state/reference/anthropic-docs/claude-code/hooks.md § SessionStart) -- never a widened firing set. guard-hook-generation-self-probe.py runs LAST and every guard's captured output is flushed to real stdout/stderr IMMEDIATELY after it runs (never accumulated for one final write) because that guard's own documented fail-open path calls os._exit(0), which would otherwise silently discard an earlier guard's already-collected output — see sessionstart-dispatch.py's own module docstring for the full reasoning. NOT folded here: sweep-boot.py (own 30s-timeout registration, unchanged, immediately below — an explicit handoff instruction that its timeout must not hide behind a short one) and the two hooks that were already async:true (session-start-register-doe-claude-root.py, session-start-repair-prepare-commit-msg-hook.py — folding an async hook into this SYNC dispatcher would force it to block session start, a real behaviour change; they fold into sessionstart-async-dispatch.py instead, two entries below). Timeout 10s: the max individual folded-guard timeout was 8s (guard-hook-generation-self-probe.py); 10s gives brief sequential headroom while every folded guard is documented cheap-by-construction / near-zero-subprocess on its fast path. AMENDED 2026-08-18 -- THE 'HOSTING CHANGE ONLY, NEVER A POLICY CHANGE' CLAIM ABOVE NO LONGER DESCRIBES THE WHOLE ARRAY: day-branch-assert.py (chunk C4a of docs/plans/2026-08-18-enforce-day-branch-cut-tree-invariant.md) is the first genuinely git-MUTATING leg folded into this fan-in -- it cuts the day branch when the tree sits on `main`, which is a policy act, not a banner. Authorised by the PM ruling of 2026-08-18 ('we cut automatically if we're on main. we warn if we are on a branch that is not compliant with our auto-push rules'); recorded so this does not read as an undocumented contract break. It is registered `startup` ONLY and MUST STAY THAT WAY -- compact/resume/fork fire mid-execution and a cut there is the mid-execution mutation doctrine keeps out of bounds. MEASURED boot cost, correcting an earlier estimate that read `one `git branch --show-current` on the early-return path`: that estimate was wrong by an order of magnitude. On the COMPLIANT (non-`main`) path -- the overwhelmingly common one -- this guard costs 4149ms cold / ~1100ms warm and emits ZERO output, because the shim resolves the engine root, imports `coordinator_core.{hooks.day_branch_assert,machine_resolver,daily_day}`, and runs the full `assert_day_branch()` BEFORE anything establishes that the branch is already compliant. Warm split: engine import 193ms, `compute_machine()` 317ms, `assert_day_branch()` 580ms. It is 96% of this whole SYNC fan-in's cost (4149ms of 4302ms across all eight startup guards) and therefore 96% of what this array contributes to interactive boot latency. A cheap pre-gate reclaims nearly all of it without changing semantics on any non-compliant path: read `.git/HEAD` directly and return early only for a `work/*` branch with no pending-push record -- `case_b_verdict`'s own compliance definition. It does NOT consult the machine id or `local_day()`; those feed only the on-`main` cut arm (`_case_a`), which the pre-gate never reaches. Do not restore the old one-git-call claim; it was never true. The local `checkout -b` still applies on the rare lock-winner path, and the network push is still queued to the async fan-in below, deliberately kept out of this array's shared 10s budget.

SessionStart._comment: C1b EM-role assertion (assert-em-role.py), UNFOLDED from the SESSIONSTART-DISPATCH FAN-IN above back into its own top-level registration (chunk C1, docs/plans/2026-08-29-restore-em-boot-payload-delivery.md). Measured across 279 archived session transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/X--DoE-claude/ carrying the `# EM Operating Doctrine` marker: the payload reached a session's actual context (attachment.content) in only 4 while riding the fan-in's single shared stdout stream -- in the other 275 it existed only in the transcript's untruncated attachment.stdout record, captured then truncated away before becoming context. Restored as its own top-level entry rather than reordered to run first inside the fan-in: a reorder would make delivery depend on no sibling leg in that process ever growing its own output, which is the same fragility relocated, not fixed. A dedicated registration gives this payload its own stdout stream and therefore its own preview window, independent of every other guard. Positive control for this shape: sweep-boot.py immediately below is an existing top-level SessionStart registration firing on the same event, and its output reaches a session's `content` field in 104 of the last 120 archived sessions, at lengths well over 2 KB. Matcher preserved EXACTLY as the fan-in declared it: `startup|resume|clear|compact|fork` -- widening or narrowing it is a behaviour change this chunk does not authorise. Accepted cost: this adds back roughly one python3 cold start (~150-230ms, extrapolated from state/audits/2026-08-16-doe-spawn-totality-kill-list.md's per-interpreter figures) to SessionStart, taking that 2026-08-16 fan-in's net saving from -10 to -9 processes -- its own ratified rationale was pure process-count reduction and never depended on preserving any leg's own delivery channel, so this does not reverse that decision on its own terms. See test_sessionstart_em_role_registered.py for the registration pin.

Stop._comment: STOP-DISPATCH FAN-IN (state/audits/2026-08-16-doe-hook-consolidation-feasibility.md) -- the single Stop entrypoint, replacing the five standalone registrations that used to live in this array: C1a idle-EM-awareness (runtime-tripwire-em-check.py), the harness-directive dispatch nudge (nudge-harness-directive-dispatch.py, docs/wiki/harness-directive-conflicts.md), the unrouted-sizing nudge (nudge-unrouted-sizing.py, docs/wiki/coordinator-tripwires.md § NUDGE-UNROUTED-SIZING), the C3 undischarged-next-move watchdog Stop leg (watchdog-undischarged-next-move.py -- its OTHER registration, PostToolUse(Skill|Agent), is untouched), and the C5 manufactured-blocker guard (guard-manufactured-blocker.py, docs/plans/2026-08-10-posture-scaled-autonomous-disposition.md). Hosting change only, never a policy change: stop-dispatch.py runs all five predicates in one interpreter via a registry + lazy-scope-descriptor pattern copied from preuse-write-dispatch.py/_guard_runner.py, with per-guard try/except BaseException fail-open isolation and CONCATENATE-ALL aggregation (same contract as _stop_family_runner.py) -- see that module's own docstring for the full guard-by-guard mapping. MEASURED 5 processes/477.9ms -> 1 process/110.7ms on the all-miss path (4.3x). C2b's asyncRewake stop-watcher stays stood-down exactly as before (see stop-dispatch.py for the restore procedure, carried over verbatim from this array's former empty-hooks entry). A SIXTH entry was added after the measured figure above was taken: stop-em-report-altitude.py, the DoE-side wiring for the EM->PM comms-budget advisory engine op hooks.em_report_altitude (state/dispatch-briefs/2026-08-29-structural-ten-bullet-cap-on-em-messages/C1.md) -- see that shim's own docstring for its plain-text, always-exit-0, non-blocking channel contract. A group-em-park-spool.py entry was added later still: the Group-EM wake's PRODUCER, appending one line to the spool the fleet watch drains whenever this session's own park verdict lands. It is registered LAST in stop-dispatch.py's REGISTRY and deliberately AFTER receiver-state-sensor.py, whose write is the verdict it reports -- that order is load-bearing and moving it earlier spools the previous turn's verdict, silently. Like the sensor it always exits 0 with empty stdout, so it contributes nothing to the CONCATENATE-ALL aggregation and can never change a verdict; it takes no Stop entry of its own purely to avoid a second interpreter cold start on every Stop fleet-wide.

SessionEnd._comment: Best-effort archival of this session's coordinator-sessions bookkeeping dir (nudge sentinels, dispatch evidence, started_at, meta.json), moved HERE from the /workstream-complete ceremony because that ceremony fires mid-session -- a session can close several workstreams before it actually ends, and archiving there reset once-per-session guards a still-live session still needed. SessionEnd fires exactly once, when the session is genuinely over. Matcher '' fires on every SessionEnd reason (clear, logout, prompt_input_exit, other) -- archival is wanted regardless of why the session ended. Shells out to the claude-klabauter-resident coordinator/bin/archive-session-scope.py archive-session --sid <sid> CLI (already non-fatal-by-design; see that script's own module docstring) rather than importing coordinator_core.session.scope directly, so this repo has exactly one thin caller of an entrypoint claude-klabauter already built for this call. Fails silently in every direction (unparsable stdin, absent session_id, unresolvable claude-klabauter root, subprocess timeout/failure) -- the 24h reaper is the documented backstop, so this hook must never block session teardown. Never falls back to a pid-derived or guessed session key. FLIPPED to type "http" (C6, docs/plans/2026-09-02-flip-four-hook-registrations-onto-http.md), calling hooks.sessionend_archive_session -- deletes TWO cold spawns per session close (this hook's own interpreter start plus the archive-session-scope.py subprocess it used to shell out to), on a hook firing once per session across ~20 concurrent sessions. SHIPPING WITH A KNOWN DEFECT, ON THE PM'S EXPLICIT CALL ("Ship both", 2026-09-02) -- against the engine this fleet resolves to today (the published klabauter mirror), every fire surfaces a harness validation error (hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName: "SessionEnd" is not in the harness enum) and the op's injected output is dropped; see 2026-09-02 spike record (docs/plans/2026-09-02-flip-four-hook-registrations-onto-http.md spike leg 4) and C4's memo. The archival side-effect still runs -- the op executes; only the reply fails validation -- and the 24h reaper remains the documented backstop, so nothing durable is lost. This defect disappears once claude-klabauter@d93f731fe5 (or later) reaches the published mirror: it omits hookSpecificOutput for EVENTS_REJECTING_HOOK_SPECIFIC_OUTPUT (frozenset({"SessionEnd"})) and hoists additionalContext top-level. Even post-fix, no additionalContext/systemMessage surfaces here: SessionEnd is terminal, there is no subsequent model turn to splice context into -- the fix removes operator-facing error noise and nothing more. RE-CHECK TRIGGER: EM re-checks at the next cadence gate after this plan lands, confirming the validation error appears exactly as characterised (no archival loss, no session-teardown block) and confirming C4's memo has an answer; if claude-klabauter has not answered by the second cadence gate, REVERT per the shape below rather than letting the degradation become the status quo. TO REVERT (not symmetric with the flip): set type back to "command" AND restore the command key -- command: "python3" -- that this flip dropped; args stays either way. A revert that only flips type yields a command registration with no command, which runs nothing -- silent total loss, strictly worse than the degraded state it was meant to undo.

SubagentStart._comment: C3 (docs/plans/2026-08-10-adopt-harness-native-hook-capabilities.md) -- moves the dispatched-agent bookkeeping WRITE onto SubagentStart, the first event carrying a real agent_id/agent_type identity pair, replacing the regex-scrape last resort the PostToolUse(Agent) leg used when both tool_response.agentId/.agent_id were absent. This call sends agent_id AND the real agent_type (track-dispatched-agents.py branches on hook_event_name), falling back to the literal "unknown" only when the payload carries no usable type. It formerly sent that placeholder unconditionally, so the row would land on the engine's enrich-in-place branch (coordinator_core/hooks/track_dispatched_agents.py::_resolve_row_collision) when PostToolUse(Agent) supplied type and model together. That is now inverted deliberately: PostToolUse(Agent) never fires for a Workflow agent() spawn, so the placeholder persisted permanently on exactly those rows, and the two guards keyed on column 3 failed in opposite directions off it -- the plan-body deny could not key (fail-open) while the sanctioned commit agent was refused as an unrostered type (fail-closed). Verified live: a workflow-spawned row read agent_id/unknown/unknown before this change and agent_id/unknown/coordinator:test-runner after. Cost, accepted knowingly and measured on live rows: on the RAW-AGENT-ID path the enrich call now matches on type, takes the resolver's dedup arm, and its model is dropped -- a built-in-type dispatch reading "<id> claude-sonnet-5 Explore" before this change reads "<id> unknown Explore" after; rows keyed by a named agent id are unaffected and still carry a real model. No consumer branches on that string (runtime-tripwire watchers fall through to their opus-default threshold; session-LoE undercounts opus dispatches), so it costs estimate quality, never correctness. Sender (claude-klabauter-em, 2026-08-18) reports this gate closed on their side. The resolver's AMBIGUOUS arm did not fire in a post-change sweep spanning coordinator:* and built-in types; on a future spelling mismatch, normalize both sides at the comparison rather than restoring the placeholder. The PostToolUse(Agent) registration below is unchanged in shape; it still writes, now purely as the enrichment call. Column 4 (timestamp) is deliberately set here, nearer the true dispatch moment, and preserved by the enrich branch rather than overwritten. Failure mode (Review: coordinator:code-reviewer, Finding 5): if the PostToolUse(Agent) enrich fire never lands for a given agent (state/bug-backlog/2026-08-10-posttooluse-agent-does-not-fire-for-some-8c1d40be9f2a.yaml documents this happens), this create call's placeholder row -- subagent_type="unknown", dispatched_model="unknown" -- now persists PERMANENTLY instead of the dispatch going unrecorded as it did pre-C3. Accepted tradeoff: a permanently-unknown row beats a dispatch recorded nowhere, but it means a future reader diagnosing stale "unknown" rows in dispatched-agents.txt cannot distinguish 'genuinely unresolved' from 'enrich never fired' without checking the linked bug. THE SHIM NOW CARRIES TWO OPS via dispatch_ops_from_hook: the bookkeeping op above runs FIRST, then the catering op, because the catering op reads back through dispatched-agents.txt and needs the bookkeeping write already landed. Catering moved here from PreToolUse(Agent) because that event has no agent_id and never fires for a Workflow agent() spawn. This is deliberately NOT a second SubagentStart entry: a second entry would price a second permanent python3 cold start (~642ms fleet-wide) against DR-344's 500ms brightline -- riding the existing shim avoids that.

SubagentStop._comment: Stage 1 of the mechanical zero-tool-use subagent detector (docs/plans/2026-07-25-zero-tool-use-detection.md, C1/C2) -- fires on every subagent completion, reads the payload's agent_transcript_path (never the decoy transcript_path -- see the plan's AC10/Pinned contract), and relays to the coordinator_core.hooks.subagent_zero_tool_use claude-klabauter op, which counts tool_use blocks and writes the durable detection record. It relays a SECOND op in the same in-process dispatch_ops_from_hook call -- coordinator_core.hooks.subagent_review_mark, which derives a commit-ledger review mark from a finishing reviewer's own reviewed_range findings. That op is deliberately NOT a second SubagentStop entry in this file: a second entry would buy a second permanent python3 cold start (the ~642ms priced below) on every subagent stop fleet-wide, where folding it into this entry's existing call adds no process at all. Per-op errors are returned by that seam rather than raised, so neither op can suppress the other -- which is what makes it safe for the review-mark op to be registered here while a published engine mirror predating it still resolves the method to a returned error. Emits nothing (DEC-4: a SubagentStop hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext reaches only the subagent's own context, never the EM's -- Stage 2, folded into the existing UserPromptSubmit runtime-tripwire-em-check.py entry below, is what surfaces it). Registered LAST, only after the claude-klabauter op landed (claude-klabauter commit 82224422) -- an unregistered script is inert; a registered one that silently no-ops on every SubagentStop until the op exists is the exact fail-open-reads-as-healthy shape this workstream exists to kill. This registration percolates to every OSS install of the coordinator plugin, most of which have no claude-klabauter and therefore no engine op to resolve -- for those installs this is a permanent per-SubagentStop python3 cold start (~642ms on the reference Windows machine) that can only ever no-op, same as the other _engine_root-gated entries in this file; precedented, not a blocker, but named here rather than shipped silently.

UserPromptExpansion._comment: mise-en-place run-id auto-mint (the mise-side twin of the pickup-autofire entry above). Fires ahead of UserPromptSubmit on a `mise-en-place` verb invocation; the script matches command_name (same bare-verb-vs-namespaced normalization as pickup-autofire.py), mints a fresh Phase-0 run id through the engine plane's `backlog-grind-assemble mint-run-id mise-en-place` CLI, immediately briefs that same id back through `backlog-grind-assemble brief mise-en-place --run-id <minted>`, and injects the minted id, its implied (not-yet-existing) inventory path, and the brief's decision object as additionalContext. Every failure mode (unresolvable CLI, non-zero exit, timeout, malformed JSON, missing keys) degrades to silent pass -- this hook never blocks /mise-en-place; a failed mint just means the EM mints by hand, today's behaviour. Provenance: engine-plane commit 339470fd6bd7 shipped the mint-run-id verb; cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-04-claude-klabauter-em-mint-run-id-verb-shipped.md pins the consumer contract this hook relies on.

UserPromptExpansion._comment: handoff residue-segment retrieval seam (third UserPromptExpansion entry). Fires on a `handoff` verb invocation (same bare-verb-vs-namespaced normalization as pickup-autofire.py/mise-autofire.py); computes the active case set for coordinator/skills/handoff/residue/'s segment contract (`shared` unconditionally, `dirty-tree` from a read-only `git status --porcelain`, `predecessor`/`carried-items` from the read-only `baton-assemble brief handoff` CLI, self-resolving to this session's own held handoff claim), selects every segment whose `case` is active, sorts ascending by `order`, and injects the concatenated bodies as additionalContext -- so the EM never hand-opens a segment file. Read-only end to end: `apply` is never invoked from this hook and there is no mutating half. async:false because the segment set must land in the SAME turn the EM's /handoff prompt is being expanded into. Every failure mode (unresolvable baton-assemble binary, non-zero exit, timeout, malformed JSON, missing/unreadable residue directory, a single malformed segment) degrades to silent pass -- this hook never blocks /handoff, which fires under context pressure by definition. Budget-capped (see `_CONTEXT_BUDGET_CHARS` in the script's own module docstring for the exact figure -- deliberately NOT the 10,000 chars pickup-autofire.py/mise-autofire.py carry), degrading class:droppable segments before ever touching a class:protected one. Install-surface note: this hook type required /reload-plugins to start firing during the spike that proved the mechanism (see pickup-autofire.py's own module docstring for the same finding) -- a plain hooks.json edit alone was not observed to be enough on its own.

UserPromptExpansion._comment: Group EM entry auto-fire (fourth UserPromptExpansion entry). Fires ahead of UserPromptSubmit on a `group-em` verb invocation; the script matches command_name (same bare-verb-vs-namespaced normalization as pickup-autofire.py/mise-autofire.py), runs coordinator/bin/group-em-enter.py --json, and injects the standing verdict, roster, digest and baseline as additionalContext -- so the mode is entered by the time the session's own turn starts, rather than assembled from SKILL.md by hand.
